data.title: Backdrop Blur
data.tagline: Blur the content behind a translucent surface
data.description: Backdrop blur creates a frosted-glass effect by blurring what is behind a partly transparent element. It can separate a floating header or overlay while keeping context visible. Always provide enough background color and contrast, because blur support and source imagery vary.

use: Separate a layer without fully hiding the background
avoid: Place low-contrast text over unpredictable images
Apply strong blur to many nested surfaces
Rely on blur as the only boundary
Ignore browsers or devices where the effect is limited

lessonPractice.title: A sticky navigation needs a glass effect, but its background is fully opaque and low-end phones stutter while scrolling. What should change?

options.label: Combine a translucent surface with restrained blur and provide a readable solid-color fallback
options.feedback: Transparency exposes content to the backdrop filter, while limited scope and fallback protect performance and readability.

options.label: Keep the opaque background and continue increasing the backdrop-blur radius
options.feedback: An opaque surface hides the scene behind it, so increasing backdrop blur cannot produce visible glass.

options.label: Extend heavy blur across the whole page so every region uses the same style
options.feedback: Large layered blur increases rendering cost and removes clear boundaries from body content and states.

data.agentPrompt: Use a translucent surface and restrained backdrop blur for the sticky navigation, keeping text readable over every scrolled background. Fall back to a clear solid surface when unsupported or slow, and test low-end mobile, dark mode, and layered overlays.
